privacyPage.title: Privacy Policy
privacyPage.lead: This policy explains how WATAD Software («WATAD», «we») collects, uses, stores, and protects personal data when you visit watadiq.com, use WATAD ONE, or work with us as a client.
privacyPage.manageCookiesHint: You can reopen the cookie banner and change your choices at any time.

cookieRows.purpose: Site security, language, session, WATAD ONE sign-in, cookie consent storage.
Understand traffic and improve pages (only if you allow).
Measure campaigns and show relevant offers (only if you allow).

intro.title: Introduction
paragraphs: We respect your privacy and aim to be transparent about the data we process. This policy applies to watadiq.com, WATAD ONE identity services, and related products operated by WATAD Software.
By using our website or services, you acknowledge this policy. Where consent is required (for example non-essential cookies), we ask before enabling those features.

controller.title: Data controller
paragraphs: WATAD Software is the data controller for personal data described in this policy.
Contact: info@watadiq.com Website: https://www.watadiq.com

collect.title: Information we collect
bullets: Account data: email, display name, profile fields when you create a WATAD ONE account.
Authentication data: passkey metadata, session identifiers, device labels, sign-in timestamps.
Developer data: organization name, app names, OAuth client IDs, redirect URIs, team invitations.
Usage data: pages visited, browser type, IP address (truncated where possible), referral URLs.
Communication data: messages you send via contact forms or email.
Cookie preferences: your cookie consent choices stored locally on your device.

cookies.title: Cookies & similar technologies
cookies.lead: We use cookies and local storage to run the site, remember language, and, only with your permission, analytics or marketing tools.
paragraphs: Essential cookies are always active because the site cannot function without them. You control optional categories from the cookie banner or the button at the bottom of this page.

watadOne.title: WATAD ONE identity platform
paragraphs: WATAD ONE provides Sign in with WATAD (OAuth 2.0 / OpenID Connect) for third-party applications. When you authorize an app, we share only the scopes you approve (such as email or profile).
Developers register applications in the developer console. OAuth tokens, refresh tokens, and audit logs are processed on api.watadiq.com with industry-standard security controls.
watadOne.note: You can revoke app access anytime from your WATAD ONE account Connected apps.

legal.title: Legal bases for processing
bullets: Contract: delivering projects, accounts, and services you request.
Legitimate interests: securing our platform, preventing abuse, improving products.
Consent: non-essential cookies, optional marketing communications.
Legal obligation: responding to lawful requests when required.

use.title: How we use your information
bullets: Provide and maintain watadiq.com and WATAD ONE.
Authenticate users and protect accounts (passkeys, email codes, sessions).
Operate developer features: apps, webhooks, audit logs, team access.
Respond to inquiries and support requests.
Analyze aggregated usage to improve performance (with consent where required).
Comply with law and enforce our terms.

sharing.title: Sharing & processors
paragraphs: We do not sell personal data. We share data only with trusted processors who help us operate the service (hosting, email delivery, security/CDN), under contracts that require appropriate safeguards.
OAuth applications you authorize receive data according to the scopes shown on the consent screen.

retention.title: Data retention
bullets: Account data: kept while your account is active and for a reasonable period after deletion for security and legal purposes.
Session and auth logs: typically 90 days to 24 months depending on security needs.
Developer audit logs: retained for security and compliance review.
Cookie consent: stored locally until you clear browser storage or change preferences.

security.title: Security
paragraphs: We use HTTPS/TLS, HttpOnly session cookies for WATAD ONE, PKCE for OAuth public clients, rate limiting, audit logging, and infrastructure protections (WAF/CDN). No method is 100% secure; we continuously improve our controls.

rights.title: Your rights
bullets: Access, correction, or deletion of your personal data where applicable.
Withdraw consent for optional cookies or marketing.
Revoke third-party app access from your WATAD ONE dashboard.
Object to or restrict certain processing under applicable law.
Lodge a complaint with a supervisory authority in your country.
rights.note: To exercise rights, email info@watadiq.com. We may need to verify your identity.

children.title: Children
paragraphs: Our services are not directed at children under 16. We do not knowingly collect data from children. Contact us if you believe a child provided personal data.

changes.title: Changes to this policy
paragraphs: We may update this policy when our practices or legal requirements change. We will post the new version on this page with an updated date. Significant changes may be announced on the website.

about.intro: WATAD is an official Iraqi software agency specializing in web development, mobile applications, cybersecurity, and digital products that help bold brands grow.

sections.title: Our story
paragraphs: WATAD was founded to give Iraqi businesses and creators the same caliber of digital craftsmanship found in global tech hubs. We combine sharp design, reliable engineering, and security first thinking so every product we ship feels premium and performs under pressure.
From startups launching their first app to established brands refreshing their web presence, we partner closely with clients, translating ambitious ideas into shipped software.

devGuide.title: WATAD ONE integration guide
devGuide.lead: This guide explains how to add Sign in with WATAD to your website or app using OAuth 2.0 and OpenID Connect with PKCE.
devGuide.ctaHint: Open the developer console, create an app, then follow the steps in this guide.

flowSteps.title: Redirect user
flowSteps.text: Send the user to /oauth/authorize with client_id, redirect_uri, and PKCE challenge.

flowSteps.title: Sign in
flowSteps.text: If not signed in, they authenticate with WATAD ONE (passkey or email code).

flowSteps.title: Consent
flowSteps.text: They see your app name and requested scopes, Allow or Deny.

flowSteps.title: Callback
flowSteps.text: After approval, the user returns to redirect_uri with an authorization code.

flowSteps.title: Token exchange
flowSteps.text: Your app posts code + code_verifier to /oauth/token and receives access + ID tokens.

redirectRules: Redirect URI must match exactly what you registered in the console, including https and the /callback path.
Local dev: http://localhost:3000/callback or http://127.0.0.1:5173/callback is allowed.
No wildcards, register each environment (dev / prod) separately.
After adding a new URI, wait a few seconds before testing sign-in.

scopeRows.desc: Required, enables OpenID Connect and returns an ID token.
Display name and basic profile fields.

faq.q: redirect_uri mismatch, what do I do?
faq.a: Ensure the URI in your OAuth request matches exactly what's registered in the console. See the Redirect URIs section in this guide.
Copy Client ID from your app page in the console. Make sure the app is enabled.
Store code_verifier before redirecting to authorize and send the same value when exchanging the code at /oauth/token.
Token exchange should run on your server or same registered origin, never expose client_secret in a public SPA.

overview.title: Overview
overview.lead: WATAD ONE is an identity provider at api.watadiq.com that integrates with any site or app via OAuth 2.0 / OIDC standards.
paragraphs: When a user clicks Sign in with WATAD in your app, they're sent to watadiq.com to sign in and consent, then return to your app with a code you exchange for secure tokens.
For public clients (SPAs, mobile) use PKCE without a client secret. For confidential server apps you may use a client secret.

prerequisites.title: Prerequisites
bullets: WATAD ONE account, sign in at watadiq.com/pass/login
Organization in the developer console, /pass/console
Registered app with Client ID and at least one Redirect URI
HTTPS in production (localhost allowed for development)

console.title: Developer console setup
paragraphs: 1. Open the developer console and create your organization (name + slug).
2. Create a new app, choose Public for websites/SPAs, or Confidential for servers.
3. From the app page: copy Client ID, add Redirect URIs, and customize logo/brand color for the consent screen.
4. Copy the integration snippet from the app page or use the examples in this guide.
console.note: Client secret is shown once on create or rotate, store it in secure environment variables.

redirects.title: Redirect URIs, where users return
redirects.lead: The redirect URI is where users land after consent. Any tiny mismatch causes redirect_uri mismatch errors.
paragraphs: Production example: https://myapp.com/auth/callback
Dev example: http://localhost:3000/auth/callback

flow.title: OAuth flow (Authorization Code + PKCE)
flow.lead: This is the recommended standard flow for modern applications.

spa.title: Connect a website or SPA (React, Vue, etc.)
spa.lead: Use PKCE in the browser. Never put client secret in frontend code.
paragraphs: After receiving tokens, validate the ID token via JWKS or the userinfo endpoint.
Store access tokens in memory or HttpOnly cookies, avoid localStorage for sensitive tokens.

server.title: Connect a server app (Confidential)
server.lead: For backends that can safely store a client secret.
paragraphs: Post authorization code + client_secret + code_verifier to /oauth/token from your server only.
Use environment variables for CLIENT_ID and CLIENT_SECRET.

tokens.title: Authorize URL, template
tokens.lead: Replace YOUR_CLIENT_ID, PKCE_CHALLENGE, and RANDOM state with real values.

scopes.title: Scopes
scopes.lead: Request only what your app needs. Users see each scope on the consent screen.

consent.title: Consent screen
paragraphs: On first sign-in or new scopes, users see a consent screen with your app name, logo, and permissions.
Customize logo and brand color in Developer console App Branding.
Users can revoke access later at /pass/account Connected apps.

test.title: Testing your integration
bullets: From your app page in the console: try sign-in or open the Authorize URL manually.
Verify your callback receives code and state.
Exchange the code for tokens and confirm userinfo or ID token decode.
Try Deny and ensure your app handles cancellation.
